data.body:
Root cause confirmed by experiment on macOS (no Windows runner needed).

Observation: `git remote add origin 'C:\Users\x\origin.git'` stores `url = C:\\Users\\x\\origin.git` in config. Git escapes each backslash in a config value; `remote get-url` returns the unescaped form. `tests/_topology_template.py` rebases copied paths by byte replacement using only the native (`C:\Users\...`) and forward-slash (`C:/Users/...`) spellings, so neither matches the config text. The remote URL is left pointing at the source topology's `origin.git`. Worktree pointer files (`.git`, `gitdir`) are written by git with forward slashes, so they were rewritten correctly, which matches the d724 observation.

Reproduction: a backslash is legal in a POSIX directory name. Running the test with `--basetemp` under a directory named `back\slash` fails on macOS with the same assertion as the Windows sweep ("the copied store still pushes to its template topology's origin"). With a plain basetemp it passes.

Fix (test helper only): apply the escaped spelling of each rewrite to git config files (`config`, `config.worktree` next to a `HEAD`), and only to them. A first attempt that added the escaped pair globally broke the first copy, because the escaped destination landed in the raw-spelling pointer files. `_assert_source_paths_absent` now checks the escaped source spelling in config files as well; before, it could not see this leak. The test is parametrized with a `backslash` case that fails without the fix and passes with it. make verify is running; Gerrit change to follow.

Unverified: the Windows sweep itself. The next Windows advisory sweep after merge is the direct check.
